_note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the whole site — the only data file in the app. Shaped as DB TABLES, not as a tree: `layouts` and `hotspots` are sibling arrays and a hotspot names its parent with `layoutId` (the foreign key). The nesting the Resources panel shows is rebuilt at load by src/config/index.ts, and the engine's scene/destination structure is projected at import by src/shared/scene-data/adapter.ts — nothing is generated to disk, so no value exists here twice. Each top-level key maps to one table or one settings row: meta/assets/world/cameras/lights/globals are the site record, zones/tones/copy are its presentation, layouts and hotspots are the two content tables.

assets._note: TWO MODELS, ONE ZONE. `modelUrl` is the DOLLHOUSE model — a decimated whole-zone GLB drawn in one go, which is the right answer for a fixed vantage that frames everything at once. The walking view does not use it: it streams the chunk set in `stream` instead. `previewUrl` is the point-cloud silhouette shown behind the loading HUD and must be baked FROM `modelUrl` — it is that model dissolving in, so a preview of any other mesh draws a cloud at the wrong scale and in the wrong place. 60,000 points, bounds x -2156..-64 / z -875..969, which is the 25-compressed GLB's own extent. There is no `navmeshUrl` here: the bake emits the navmesh alongside the chunks, so it travels with them (and follows NEXT_PUBLIC_ASSET_BASE to a CDN) rather than being a second copy someone has to keep in step. Set it only for a site with no `stream` block.

_note: ADAPTIVE CHUNK STREAMING — THE WALKING VIEW ONLY. The model is cut into
831 object chunks, each baked at three quality tiers, and the distance
from the camera decides which tier a chunk is loaded at — or whether it
is loaded at all.
near = good · mid = medium · far = low · beyond far = not loaded
The DOLLHOUSE does not stream: it draws `assets.modelUrl`, one decimated
whole-zone GLB. Streaming is a bad trade from a fixed vantage that frames
the entire zone — the view cone covers everything, so the frustum cull
buys nothing and the bands only fight the byte ceiling, whose eviction
drops the FURTHEST chunk first, i.e. exactly the half of the frame the
shot is composed around. The streamer mounts on the way in to first
person, under the entry blackout, and fills in around `cameras.spawn`
before the fade lifts.
The asset set is baked in the LA_PORT_ADAPTIVE repo (`npm run bake
portla-c5-v4-obj`) and staged under public/assets/<slug>/assets/, which
is gitignored — set NEXT_PUBLIC_ASSET_BASE to serve it from a CDN.
NO PALETTE, NO ANIMATED RIG. v4-obj is the plain object-chunked bake of
la-port-zone-c5-model-v4.glb: `chunking.instancing` and `animation` are
both off, so there is no palette.glb, no instances.bin and no
animated.glb to preload. Every byte the scene holds is a chunk under the
LRU — nothing is permanently resident — and the crane rigs ship inside
the chunks as ordinary static geometry, frozen in their rest pose. The
instance and animation paths in the runtime stay inert (both init calls
no-op on a 404), which is exactly what they were written to do.
Only `tiers.*.distance`, `tiers.*.texture`, `streaming.*`, `cache.*` and
`fog` are read live by the browser — edit and reload. The geometry LODs,
the texture rungs and the chunking itself are baked into files and need a
re-bake over in that repo.
MEASURED on this asset set: 26,284 primitive-units / 12,766,071 tris ->
25,999 objects -> 831 chunks, all 831 carrying geometry. 94 MB of chunk
GLBs + 37 MB of texture rungs, 70 images, 612 materials. Near-tier tris
reconcile exactly against the source. Worst case at these bands (360°, no
frustum cull): peak 11.40 M tris, 24.9 MB encoded, 360 MB decoded,
38.6 MB of WebP texture VRAM — ~399 MB total. With the frustum cull on,
the real resident set is roughly a third of that.
_bands: WHY far IS 900 AND NOT 300, i.e. why geometry looked missing.
The 50/150/300 bands came from the original 2.1 x 1.9 km portla-c5. This
is a 15 x 10 km district cut into OBJECT chunks, whose sizes vary
enormously: radius p10 3.6 m, p50 19 m, p90 112 m, p99 692 m. A chunk
loads by the distance to its SURFACE, so a big object is credited with
its own size and outlives a small object standing on it — by a mean of
1355 m over the 4055 co-located pairs in this manifest. That is the whole
bug: the canopy renders and its poles do not, the stack renders and its
containers do not. Nothing is missing from the bake.
MEASURED, 150 ground cameras, 360° (worst case). A HOLE is an object
whose own chunk is absent while a building-scale chunk covering the same
spot is present:
near/mid/far   resident   encoded   chunk tris   HOLES
Holes fall 98%, and 11.3 MB still sits well under residentBudgetMB.
mid 250 (was 150) costs +0.3 MB and keeps the 150-250 m ring off the far
tier, which is simplifyRatio 0.15 — raising far without raising mid would
have put most of the visible world at the coarsest LOD.
The other half of the fix is in the runtime, not here: ChunkManager
measures surface distance to the bounding BOX rather than the bounding
SPHERE (the sphere is the half-diagonal, so it wildly over-credits
anything elongated). Worth ~a quarter of the total; the BANDS are what
actually closed the gap.

cache._note: Sized on AVERAGE cost per entry, not worst case: 831 chunks / 2493 lod urls, avg 454 KB decoded per entry, so 500 projects to ~222 MB of JS heap. The 360°-no-cull estimate says peak mounted 831, but scaling by the cull ratio actually observed in the browser (82 visible vs 297 no-cull) puts the real mounted set near 229 — 500 leaves ~270 spare entries for backtracking, and still sits under the 831 total so the LRU always has something evictable. residentBudgetMB 33 = peak encoded 26.0 x1.25.

_note: THE SECOND STRATEGY over the same manifest — for the layout cameras.
Every layout here is a framing shot with `walkable: false`, authored
54-412 m up and as much as 2.8 km from the terminal. The bands above
are tuned for a person STANDING in it, so from those cameras almost
nothing resolved. Measured, box metric, per layout, chunks inside the
990 m unload radius out of 831:
L01/L02/L03/L07 got 2 chunks each — the water plane and the terrain
plane, the only two whose boxes contain the camera. Everything built
was 1.5-2.8 km away, i.e. outside the radius, so the shot framed sky.
WHY THIS IS CHEAP. The whole model at the far tier is 831 chunks /
22.0 MB encoded / 11.02 M tris, and all 70 images at the 128 px rung
total 0.1 MB. So a radius spanning the entire 15 x 10 km district costs
about 22 MB resident — under the ground config's own 33 MB ceiling.
Measured chunks resolved at far 6000: 831 of 831 from every one of the
ten cameras. Nothing about this needed a second asset set.
far 6000 rather than 4000: 4000 already reaches all ten (826-831), but
6000 spans the district corner-to-corner for the same 22.0 MB, so the
radius stops being a number anyone has to re-check when a camera moves.
near/mid are raised because at this altitude nothing is within 150 m of
the camera anyway — leaving them at 50/250 would have put the whole
frame on the far tier. 150/800 keeps what the shot is composed around
on the mid tier and only the district backdrop on far.
limitChunks 900 (> the 831 total) because all 831 are mounted at once
here: the LRU never evicts a mounted chunk, so a lower ceiling would
simply sit unenforced. The ground config's 500 takes back over on the
way down and evicts to it then.
Only the keys that DIFFER are listed. `streaming` and everything else
not named is inherited from the block above, so a retune there carries
here on its own.

spawn._note: WHERE FIRST PERSON BEGINS. Authored rather than derived from startLayoutId because every layout here is an aerial framing (walkable: false — schema-wise, not a valid first-person entry point), so there is no walkable checkpoint to derive it from; deriving it anyway put the walking start at L01's camera, 381 m up and 46 m outside the navmesh in X. VERIFIED against assets.navmeshUrl: this XZ is inside a navmesh triangle, surface Y 0.160. It is also the point the streamer fills in around while the entry blackout is up, so moving it changes what you land looking at AND what has finished loading when the fade lifts.

sky._note: The procedural sky dome (see terminal/scene/environment/sky). `mode` picks a stop on the day arc — "dusk" is the open-sea study's sunset palette, "day" its midday one, "off" restores the flat blue backdrop. `t` overrides the stop with an explicit 0..1, and ?debug=true drives it live from a slider. COLOURS ARE NOT AUTHORED HERE: the sun direction, the sun tint and the ambient tint are all derived from the same palette the sky is drawn from, so they cannot drift from it. `lights` is merged over the `lights` block above and is for INTENSITIES — how strongly the model is lit at this hour, which the study (a shader with no scene lights) has no opinion on.

map._note: TWO RECTS: zone inside site. The map opens framed on `zone` — the walkable area, the only place a click resolves to a route — lifted out of a dimmed surround. ONE image does both passes: `site` is a pre-graded aerial that already lights the terminal and darkens everything around it, so there is no second render layered over it to misregister against. A `plan` block may be added back (a top-down model render, its own bounds beside it) when the zone needs more resolution than the aerial carries. `site.bounds` names the world coords of the image EDGES: minX/maxX are its left/right (X grows rightward, east), minZ/maxZ its top/bottom (Z grows UPWARD, north) — so X reads plainly and only Z is inverted. VERIFIED twice: the lit terminal centres on the navmesh to within 2 m in X and 45 m in Z, and the spawn point lands on the quay it is authored at. `zone` is a PLAIN world rect (minX < maxX) because people author it, defaulting to the navmesh AABB.
